content.text: Chen Lu, the New Year's holiday is coming soon. Do you have any plans? I'm trying to figure out what to do with the kids—something that's relaxing but doesn't cost too much.

Fang Qing, I plan to take my son to free parks or riversides for bike rides when the weather is nice, and I can also go for a run to exercise. If the weather is bad, we’ll stay at home, where I can teach him to play chess or we can watch an old movie together. Since you nurses have fewer days off, it’s even more important to choose activities that are low-stress and easy to manage.

These ideas are really great! Cycling not only helps with physical exercise but also allows you to get closer to nature. I remember you mentioned before that the newly built greenway along the river has fewer people and beautiful scenery, making it perfect for taking the kids.
Yes, it's indeed quiet there, and the safety factor is high. I usually drive by and have observed the road conditions—it's very suitable for family activities.

I'd also like to share a few of my thoughts: Take your child to the library for free parent-child reading sessions, or bake something simple at home together, like cookies. Baking cookies at home gives children a strong sense of involvement and is healthier than store-bought ones.

Baking sounds like a lot of fun and can help develop children's hands-on skills. However, remember to remind them of the importance of washing their hands, just as you emphasized in the flu prevention tips you shared earlier.

Yes, safety first! I always incorporate health tips into activities, like wearing a helmet when cycling or washing hands before baking. It reminds me of how you emphasized similar safety awareness when organizing team training sessions before.

Exactly, it's all about community support. Speaking of low-cost activities, there are also some free museums or exhibitions in the city. My son had a great time at the science museum last time and even learned something.
The museum is a great idea! It's both entertaining and educational. I've organized some activity ideas into a mind map and sent it to you. Maybe it can give you more inspiration.
This diagram summarizes activities categorized under outdoor, indoor, and public resources, which you can refer to.

Thank you, Fang Qing. This chart is very practical! The mention of park cycling in the outdoor category perfectly aligns with my plans. The indoor category includes baking, just as you mentioned earlier. Public resources like libraries and museums are also listed, which both of us brought up.

Yes, these activities are based on the economic conditions and time constraints of ordinary people, yet they can provide high-quality parent-child bonding. Just like when we previously reviewed 'small favors we casually do,' those little things can accumulate into precious memories.

Yes, the wisdom of life lies in these ordinary choices. My son has recently become fascinated with chess, and I teach him at home. It not only exercises the mind but also doesn’t cost anything, making it a great option when the weather is bad.

Chess is indeed great; it cultivates patience and strategic thinking. When I bake with my child, I also teach them to measure ingredients, incorporating a bit of math knowledge, so that entertainment can be rewarding too.
Sounds great! After exchanging these ideas, I feel like my New Year's holiday plans have become even more enriching. Low cost doesn't mean low quality; the key is to spend quality time together.

Completely agree. Thank you for sharing, Chen Lu. Every time I chat with you, I always learn some practical life advice, just like in our past conversations where you consistently offer steady and reliable help.
Likewise, Fang Qing. Your expertise and meticulous care have also benefited me greatly. From public health incidents to everyday matters, we have always supported each other.
Yes, community support makes us all stronger. I hope everyone can enjoy these low-cost family entertainments during the New Year's holiday and relax.

Absolutely. If the weather is nice, I'll take my son biking by the river and remember to wear a helmet. If it rains, we'll stay home and play chess or watch a movie. Take care of yourself too—nursing is hard work.
Thank you for your concern! I'll take the kids to the library or do some baking, incorporating health knowledge. Wishing you a pleasant holiday and let's stay in touch!
